name: Ole-Johan Dahl
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Dahl's seminal work on Simula and object-oriented programming began in the early 1960s when he was in his early 30s; his first technical report (1957) at age 26 was a routine computing manual, not a material milestone.
early_history_summary: Dahl studied numerical mathematics at the University of Oslo and began working at the Norwegian Computing Center in the early 1960s, where he collaborated with Kristen Nygaard on the Simula languages.
family_context_summary: Son of Finn Dahl and Ingrid Othilie Kathinka Pedersen; the family fled to Sweden during the German occupation of Norway when Dahl was 13.
evidence_summary: Dahl's early career consisted of routine computing reports at the Norwegian Defence Research Establishment. His material milestone — co-creating Simula and object-oriented programming with Kristen Nygaard — came in the 1960s when he was in his early 30s. He won the Turing Award in 2001. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Maryam Mirzakhani
milestone_by_age_26: Won a gold medal at the International Mathematical Olympiad in 1994 at age 17, becoming the first Iranian woman to do so, and followed with a perfect-score gold medal in 1995.
early_history_summary: Mirzakhani grew up in Tehran and attended the NODET school for exceptional talents. She and friend Roya Beheshti made the Iranian Mathematical Olympiad team in 1994, where she won gold; she repeated with a perfect 42/42 score in 1995. She then studied at Sharif University of Technology before pursuing a PhD at Harvard under Curtis McMullen.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond her birth in Tehran, Iran.
primary_early_advantage_tags: NODET school, IMO pipeline, prodigy, Sharif University, Harvard
evidence_summary: Mirzakhani attended Tehran's Farzanegan School (NODET), a pipeline for exceptional talents. She won IMO gold at 17 (1994) and a perfect-score gold at 18 (1995), making her the first Iranian woman to achieve this. She then studied at Sharif University before her Harvard PhD (2004). Her rare mathematical ability was evident early, and the Iranian Olympiad pipeline provided structured opportunity. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Tehran, Iran; family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond her attendance at a NODET school for exceptional talents.
current_position: Died on July 14, 2017 at age 40 in Stanford, California; was a professor at Stanford University and the first woman to win the Fields Medal (2014).

trajectory.event: Won gold medal at the International Mathematical Olympiad in Hong Kong, the first Iranian woman to do so.
Won a second IMO gold medal with a perfect 42/42 score in Toronto.
Co-authored the book 'Elementary Number Theory, Challenging Problems' in Persian with Roya Beheshti.
Completed PhD at Harvard under Curtis McMullen on hyperbolic geometry and moduli spaces.
Awarded the Blumenthal Award for promising young mathematicians.
Became the first woman and first Iranian to win the Fields Medal, the highest honor in mathematics.
Died on July 14, 2017 in Stanford, California, after a battle with breast cancer.

name: Natascha Kampusch
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Kampusch is known as a kidnapping survivor; her public profile resulted from being abducted at age 10 in 1998 and escaping in 2006, not from a personal achievement or milestone by age 26.
early_history_summary: Kampusch was abducted at age 10 in Vienna in 1998 and held captive for over eight years before escaping on August 23, 2006. She later wrote a book and hosted a talk show.
family_context_summary: Raised by mother Brigitta Sirny and father Ludwig Koch in Vienna; parents separated while she was a child.
evidence_summary: Kampusch's notability derives entirely from being a crime victim. She was abducted at age 10 and held for eight years. Her escape at 18 brought media attention, but this is not a personal achievement milestone in the sense of the rubric. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Carlos Saura
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Saura's first feature film 'Los golfos' was filmed in 1959 and premiered at Cannes in 1960 when he was 28; his first documentary short 'Cuenca' (1958) at age 26 was not a material milestone. His first major award (Silver Bear) came in 1966 at age 34.
early_history_summary: Saura studied filmmaking at the IIEC in Madrid (1952-1957) and began making documentary shorts in 1955. His first documentary 'Cuenca' was completed in 1958, and his first feature 'Los golfos' premiered at Cannes in 1960.
family_context_summary: Born in Huesca, Spain; brother of painter Antonio Saura. Family background otherwise not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Brother Antonio Saura was a noted painter, suggesting an artistic family environment, but specific transfer of domain advantage is not documented.
evidence_summary: Saura studied at the IIEC film school in Madrid (1952-57) under Juan Antonio Bardem and Luis García Berlanga. His first documentary 'Cuenca' (1958) was a short, not a material career milestone. His first feature 'Los golfos' premiered at Cannes in 1960 (age 28), and his first major award (Silver Bear for 'La caza') came in 1966 (age 34). No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Waldemar Cierpinski
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Olympic marathon gold medal at the 1976 Montreal Olympics on July 31, 1976, setting an Olympic record (2:09:55), just three days before his 26th birthday.
early_history_summary: Cierpinski was born in Neugattersleben, East Germany, to Polish parents. He was originally a steeplechase runner before switching to the marathon in 1974. He was virtually unknown internationally when he won the 1976 Olympic marathon, beating favored American Frank Shorter by nearly 51 seconds.
family_context_summary: Born to Polish parents who had moved to East Germany in 1945; specific family financial or occupational background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: East German sports system, steeplechase-to-marathon transition, Olympic pipeline
evidence_summary: Cierpinski benefited from the East German state sports system, which provided structured training, coaching, and competitive pipelines. He was originally a steeplechase runner before switching to the marathon in 1974, just two years before his Olympic triumph. The East German athletic infrastructure concentrated resources on promising athletes. He has been implicated in the state-sponsored doping program, though he has not been formally stripped of medals. Family background is minimally documented.
starting_point: Born in Neugattersleben, East Germany, to Polish parents who had moved to Germany in 1945; family occupational and financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from competition in 1984; lives in Halle an der Saale, Germany; member of the German Olympic Committee and honorary member of SG WiP Goettingen 06.

trajectory.event: Switched from steeplechase to the marathon, beginning focused training in the new discipline.
Won Olympic marathon gold at the Montreal Olympics in 2:09:55, an Olympic record, beating Frank Shorter by 51 seconds.
Finished fourth in the marathon at the European Championships.
Won his second consecutive Olympic marathon gold at the Moscow Olympics, duplicating Abebe Bikila's feat.
Won bronze in the marathon at the World Championships in Helsinki.
Denied a chance at a third Olympic marathon gold by the Eastern Bloc boycott of the Los Angeles Olympics; retired from competition.

name: Jean-Paul Gaultier
milestone_by_age_26: Launched his first individual fashion collection in 1976 at age 24, having already apprenticed at Pierre Cardin, Jacques Esterel, and Jean Patou since age 18.
early_history_summary: Gaultier grew up in a Paris suburb and was introduced to fashion by his maternal grandmother. He never received formal design training but began sending sketches to couture houses as a teenager. Pierre Cardin hired him as an assistant in 1970 at age 18; he subsequently worked for Jacques Esterel and Jean Patou before launching his own collection in 1976.
family_context_summary: Only child of a bookkeeper father and a cashier mother in Arcueil, a suburb of Paris. His maternal grandmother Marie Garrabe introduced him to fashion and her corsets inspired his later designs.
parent_family_domain_summary: No direct family domain advantage in fashion; his grandmother provided cultural exposure but was not a fashion professional.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Paris fashion ecosystem, Pierre Cardin apprenticeship, grandmother influence, self-taught prodigy
evidence_summary: Gaultier grew up in suburban Paris with non-fashion-professional parents, but his grandmother introduced him to fashion. He was a self-taught prodigy who designed collections for his mother and grandmother by age 13. At 18, he was hired by Pierre Cardin, then worked for Jacques Esterel and Jean Patou, gaining direct immersion in Parisian haute couture. He launched his first individual collection in 1976 at age 24, with support from fashion editors at Elle and Marie Claire. His proximity to the Paris fashion ecosystem and early apprenticeships at major houses were key advantages.
starting_point: Born in Arcueil, a suburb of Paris; only child of a bookkeeper father and cashier mother; raised with significant influence from his maternal grandmother who introduced him to fashion.
current_position: Retired from fashion following his 50th-anniversary haute couture show at Paris Fashion Week in January 2020; remains an iconic figure in fashion design.

trajectory.event: Hired as a design assistant by Pierre Cardin after sending sketches to Parisian couture houses.
Launched his first individual collection, gaining attention from fashion editors at Elle and Marie Claire.
Founded his eponymous fashion label.
Introduced skirts for men and the iconic women's corset with cone bra, stirring controversy in the fashion world.
Designed Madonna's cone bra costumes for the Blond Ambition World Tour, achieving global cultural recognition.
Launched a line of fragrances with Classique, expanding his brand beyond fashion.
Became creative director of Hermes, a major French luxury house, serving until 2010.
Retired following his 50th-anniversary haute couture show during Paris Fashion Week in January.

name: Giuliano Gemma
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Gemma worked as a stuntman and had small/uncredited film roles from 1958, but his breakthrough starring role in 'A Pistol for Ringo' came in 1965 at age 27; no material milestone by age 26 was found.
early_history_summary: Gemma was born in Rome and first worked as a stuntman. Director Duccio Tessari offered him real acting parts starting with 'Arrivano i titani' (1962). He appeared in Visconti's 'The Leopard' (1963) in a supporting role before his Spaghetti Western breakthrough in 1965.
family_context_summary: Born in Rome, Italy; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Gemma began as a stuntman and gradually gained small acting roles from 1958. By age 26 (1964), he had supporting roles including a part in Visconti's 'The Leopard' (1963), but these were not material career milestones. His breakthrough came with starring roles in Spaghetti Westerns 'A Pistol for Ringo' and 'Blood for a Silver Dollar' in 1965 at age 27. He won a David di Donatello in 1976. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Zhang Yining
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Championship team gold at the 2000 World Championships in Kuala Lumpur at age 18, and went on to win Olympic gold medals in both singles and doubles at the 2004 Athens Olympics at age 22, becoming world #1.
early_history_summary: Zhang started playing table tennis at age 5 in Beijing, taught initially by her uncle. She joined the Beijing team at age 11 under coach Li Jun (Li Jiwei) and entered the Chinese national team by age 14. She won her first international title at the Malaysian Open in 1998 and became world #1 in January 2003.
family_context_summary: Born in Beijing to ordinary working-class parents; her mother Wang Fengying was a clerk and her father was also an ordinary worker. Her uncle served as her first table tennis coach and was instrumental in her early development.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family domain advantage in sports; parents were ordinary workers with no sports background. Her uncle, though not a professional coach, provided foundational training.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Chinese table tennis system, Beijing Shichahai Sports School, uncle coach, Li Jun mentorship, early specialization
evidence_summary: Zhang was born to ordinary working-class parents in Beijing with no sports background. Her uncle introduced her to table tennis at age 5 and served as her first coach, driving her daily across three districts to train. She joined the Beijing team at 11 under coach Li Jun, who became her long-term mentor. The Chinese national table tennis pipeline provided elite training, competition, and team infrastructure from an early age. She reached the national team by 14, won her first international title at 17, and became world #1 at 21. Her early specialization and the Chinese sports system's concentration of resources were dominant advantages.
starting_point: Born in Beijing, China, to ordinary working-class parents; her mother was a clerk and her father an ordinary worker, with no family sports background.
current_position: Retired from professional table tennis in 2009; considered one of the greatest female table tennis players in history with 4 Olympic golds and 19 World Championship medals; married and living in China.

trajectory.event: Entered the Chinese national table tennis team, achieving a childhood goal.
Won her first international title at the Malaysian Open.
Won World Championship team gold at the Kuala Lumpur World Championships.
Became world #1 in the ITTF women's singles rankings in January.
Won Olympic gold medals in both singles and doubles at the Athens Olympics.
Won World Championship singles and doubles gold at the Shanghai World Championships.
Won Olympic gold medals in singles and team events at the Beijing Olympics on home soil.
Retired from professional competition after winning World Championship singles gold in Yokohama, completing a double Grand Slam.

name: Nick Szabo
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Szabo graduated with a bachelor's in computer science from the University of Washington in 1989 at age 25; his seminal work on smart contracts came in 1994 (age 30) and bit gold in 1998 (age 34). No material milestone by age 26 was found.
early_history_summary: Szabo studied computer science at the University of Washington, graduating in 1989, and later earned a Juris Doctor from George Washington University Law School. He became known in the 1990s for his work on smart contracts and digital currency.
evidence_summary: Szabo graduated from the University of Washington in 1989 with a bachelor's degree in computer science. His influential concepts — smart contracts (1994) and bit gold (1998) — were developed in his 30s. He later earned a JD from George Washington University Law School. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found. Family background is not documented.

name: Jair da Costa
milestone_by_age_26: Was a member of Brazil's 1962 World Cup-winning squad at age 22, then won the European Cup with Inter Milan in 1964 (age 24) and scored the winning goal in the 1965 European Cup final (age 25).
early_history_summary: Da Costa started his professional career at Portuguesa in Sao Paulo in 1960. After being spotted by Inter Milan coach Helenio Herrera at the 1962 World Cup, he signed for Inter in November 1962 and became a key right winger in the legendary Grande Inter side, winning four Serie A titles and two European Cups.
family_context_summary: Born in Santo Andre, Sao Paulo, Brazil; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Brazilian football pipeline, Portuguesa, Inter Milan, Helenio Herrera, Grande Inter
evidence_summary: Da Costa emerged from the Brazilian football pipeline, starting professionally at Portuguesa in Sao Paulo at age 20. He was spotted by Inter Milan coach Helenio Herrera at the 1962 World Cup and signed for Inter, where he became a key member of the legendary Grande Inter squad. He won the World Cup with Brazil in 1962 (as a squad member), then won two European Cups (1964, 1965) and four Serie A titles with Inter. His trajectory was accelerated by Herrera's tactical system and the elite Inter ecosystem. Family background is not documented.
starting_point: Born in Santo Andre, Sao Paulo, Brazil; family occupational and financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on April 26, 2025 at age 84 in Osasco, Sao Paulo, Brazil; remembered as a key winger of Inter Milan's Grande Inter era.

trajectory.event: Began his professional career at Portuguesa in Sao Paulo, Brazil.
Was a member of Brazil's World Cup-winning squad in Chile; signed for Inter Milan in November after being spotted by coach Helenio Herrera.
Won the European Cup with Inter Milan, defeating Real Madrid in the final.
Scored the winning goal in the European Cup final against Benfica, securing Inter's second consecutive European Cup.
Won consecutive Serie A titles as part of the Grande Inter squad under Helenio Herrera.
Left Inter Milan after a second spell, having played 260 games and scored 69 goals for the club.
Died on April 26, 2025 in Osasco, Sao Paulo, Brazil.

name: Raul Julia
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Julia moved to New York in 1964 and made his off-Broadway debut that year, but his Broadway debut came in 1968 (age 28) and his first Tony nomination in 1971 (age 31); no material milestone by age 26 was found.
early_history_summary: Julia grew up in San Juan, Puerto Rico, and acted in school and college productions. Orson Bean encouraged him to move to New York, which he did in 1964. He made his New York stage debut in 'La Vida Es Sueño' (1964) and joined the New York Shakespeare Festival in 1966-67 under Joseph Papp.
family_context_summary: Born in San Juan, Puerto Rico; attended Colegio San Ignacio de Loyola. His family wanted him to become a lawyer, but he pursued acting against their wishes.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; family was reportedly well-off enough to send him to a private Jesuit school and provide a stipend in New York.
evidence_summary: Julia acted throughout school and college in Puerto Rico before moving to New York in 1964 at age 24. His early New York work consisted of off-Broadway productions and street theater. His association with Joseph Papp's New York Shakespeare Festival began in 1966-67, but his Broadway debut ('The Cuban Thing', 1968) closed after one performance. His breakthrough came with a Tony-nominated performance in 'Two Gentlemen of Verona' in 1971 at age 31. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Tom Petty
milestone_by_age_26: Released the debut album 'Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers' on November 9, 1976 on Shelter Records, with the single 'Breakdown' cracking the Top 40 in the US.
early_history_summary: Petty grew up in Gainesville, Florida, and was inspired to pursue music after seeing Elvis Presley film a movie nearby at age 10. He formed his first band the Sundowners at 14, which evolved into the Epics and then Mudcrutch. After Mudcrutch failed to chart, he formed Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers in 1976 and released their debut album that November.
family_context_summary: Born in Gainesville, Florida, the eldest of two sons of Kitty Petty, a tax office worker, and Earl Petty, a traveling salesman. His father was verbally and physically abusive and disapproved of Petty's interest in the arts. The family was working-class.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family domain advantage in music; Petty's uncle Earl Jernigan worked on an Elvis Presley movie set, which inspired Petty's interest in music, but this was not a domain transfer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Mike Campbell, Benmont Tench, Mudcrutch, Shelter Records, Denny Cordell, adversity
evidence_summary: Petty grew up in a working-class family in Gainesville, Florida, with an abusive father who opposed his artistic interests. He was inspired by seeing Elvis Presley on a movie set at age 10 through his uncle's connection. He formed bands from age 14, with future Heartbreakers Mike Campbell and Benmont Tench as key collaborators. The durable complementary team was a core advantage. Shelter Records producer Denny Cordell signed the band and produced their debut. Petty's adversity — difficult family life, lack of resources — created urgency and drive. The debut album release in November 1976 at age 26 was the qualifying milestone, with 'Breakdown' becoming a Top 40 hit.
starting_point: Born in Gainesville, Florida, the eldest son of a traveling salesman father and a tax office worker mother; working-class family with an abusive father who opposed his interest in music.
current_position: Died on October 2, 2017 at age 66 in Santa Monica, California; was a Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductee (2002) with over 80 million records sold worldwide.

trajectory.event: Formed the band Mudcrutch with future Heartbreakers Mike Campbell and Benmont Tench in Gainesville, Florida.
Released the debut album 'Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers' on Shelter Records; 'Breakdown' cracked the Top 40.
Released 'Damn the Torpedoes', which reached #2 on the Billboard 200 and sold multi-platinum, establishing the band as major stars.
Released 'Hard Promises' and fought his label over album pricing, becoming an advocate for artist rights.
Joined the Traveling Wilburys supergroup with George Harrison, Bob Dylan, Roy Orbison, and Jeff Lynne.
Inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers.
Died on October 2, 2017 in Santa Monica, California, after an accidental drug overdose.
